text:
maya: Heads-up — we had a tenant-triggered burst that saturated the burst lane and caused ~3m of degraded latency for other Dedicated tenants. Not critical but noisy.

sahil: Ugh. Do we have the logs for request admit/drop during that window?

autoscaler-bot: autoscaler: scale_event type=burst_admit added=4 gpus pool=burst-lane timestamp=1747654380

liu: I pulled traces — admission queue length hit the soft cap, then we drained but preemptions spiked. Will paste short timeline after meeting.

alex: Quick Q: was this a cold-start / warmup issue or pure admission exhaustion?

maya: Looks like admission exhaustion + delayed graceful shutdown. A couple of slots were marked draining but didn't finish teardown before new pods were scheduled, so we had transient overcommit.

sahil: So two separate problems: (1) burst protection / admission policy should prevent noisy tenant from starving others, (2) shutdown/graceful teardown needs faster eviction path.

liu: Agree. For (1) I sketched a deferral window idea — if a tenant consumes >X% of burst credits in T seconds, start deferring their additional admits for D seconds, with a slow-leak back.

alex: Sounds reasonable. Could be implemented as admission token bucket with per-tenant throttles + global headroom reservation. We already have credit accounting; just need a fast path in the admit layer.

maya: Pasted the config snippet I prototyped in the test cluster:
```
admission: 
  burst_protection: 
    enabled: true
    overuse_threshold_pct: 60  # percent of burst credits in window
    window_secs: 30
    defer_secs: 45
    slow_leak_rate: 0.5  # fraction per minute
```

sahil: Two caveats: 
- Defer policy interacts poorly with SLA-weighted queues. If deferred tenant is enterprise with high SLO, we need override.
- We must emit metrics for "deferred_admits" and reason labels.

liu: For overrides we can wire in route priority/tenant tier; the policy should be a weighted deficit instead of binary defer. E.g. deficit > threshold triggers progressive backoff.

alex: On graceful shutdown: current drain waits for in-flight requests + 30s grace. We observed stuck finalizers in ~10% of cases. Suggest adding a fast-evict flag that force-closes idle connections after N seconds and moves K inflight requests to fallback model pool.

maya: That aligns with my notes. Fast-evict only for preemption scenarios and when fallback models exist. Need to ensure KV cache state preserved or warm fallback first.

sahil: Tradeoffs: aggressive fast-evict reduces tail latency for others but increases error rate for the evicted tenant. Need rollout guard and alerting (SLO deltas).

autoscaler-bot: autoscaler: fallback_route_triggered tenant=tenant-42 fallback_model=redwood-small 1747654455

liu: Proposed follow-ups: 
- RFC PR for "deferred-burst-protection" admission filter (include metrics + tier override)
- Short patch for drain controller to implement fast-evict flag + metrics
- E2E test that simulates noisy tenant and asserts neighbors' p95 doesn't regress >10%

alex: I can take the drain controller patch.

maya: I'll open the RFC draft and add the config prototype and simulation results.

sahil: I'll own the E2E harness. Add me as reviewer on the RFC.

liu: Also recommend adding a non-customer-facing dashboard showing per-tenant burst-credit burn-rate and recent deferred admits (helps SRE during incidents).

maya: Yep — add to the list. I'll tag eng-sre in the RFC.

alex: One more thing — we should avoid adding too many knobs initially. Start with conservative defaults and a kill-switch.

maya: Agreed. Conservative rollout: enabled=false by default, enable in canary pool for 24h, then gradual ramp to prod.

sahil: ok sounds like a plan. Thanks everyone. Will coordinate E2E schedule. :thumbsup:

autoscaler-bot: note: alert("burst-protection-deferred-admits") created by sahil for canary test

maya: Filed RFC draft: https://r.redwood/ops/rfcs/def-burst-protect (WIP)

liu: I'll attach traces in the RFC + node-level logs.

alex: tagging @security for any KMS or secret handling if we modify fallback handshake.

maya: Nice. Ending thread; we'll sync in async PRs.
